Resolves #18750

🌿 A control arm expecting nothing to happen could not tell "nothing happened because the code is correct" from "nothing happened because my mutation silently did not apply" — so it was free to keep passing after it stopped testing; now those two cases have different outcomes.

```js
// before — the CONTROL arm, unchanged for its whole life
run(write('blank.mjs', SPLIT.replace('    // prose about the next key', '')));
expect(status).toBe(0);
```

`replace` returns its subject untouched when the needle is absent, and **pristine `SPLIT` draws no notice either**. Rename that comment in `SPLIT` and the arm asserts `status === 0` against an unmutated fixture — passing forever, testing nothing, still titled `CONTROL:`.

Evidence: **L2** (the arm executed at head; the guard executed against a deliberately drifted needle; full unit suite) → L2 required, since the claim is about what a spec accepts and rejects. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | The mutation is assigned, then asserted against the source before the checker runs, with a message naming needle drift. |
| AC-2 | `CONTROL:` semantics intact — still `expect(status).toBe(0)` and `expect(output).not.toContain(...)`; the arm simply cannot reach them on an unmutated fixture. |
| AC-3 | **Proven falsifiable.** Needle replaced with an absent string → `exit 1`, `Error: fixture mutation changed nothing — the needle has drifted out of SPLIT`, 47 passed / 1 failed. A guard against controls that cannot fail must not ship as one. |
| AC-4 | One file, one arm. No helper module, no new `.mjs`, no other spec touched. |
| AC-5 | Full unit suite: **4119 passed, 2 skipped**. Target spec alone: 48 passed. |

## Deltas from ticket
**The ticket's central count was wrong and I corrected it before writing code — see its correction comment.** It claimed **12 mutation sites, 0 guarded**, and prescribed a shared helper plus a placement decision.

I had reproduced @neo-opus-ada's 12 by running the same syntactic pattern and called that independent verification. It was not: **her claim was about mutation arms, my check was about a substring.** Read in context, **11 of the 12 are ordinary string normalisation** — `withoutComments` stripping SCSS comments (`dockSplitterLayering:56,57`), selector normalisation (`dockRailTabLayering:72,122`), path rewriting (`esmDistTransforms:364,365`, `dockSplitterLayering:173`), gitignore pattern normalisation (`gitignoreNegationReachability:62,62,67,117`) — precisely the category the ticket's own Out of Scope excluded.

**One fixture mutation exists in this tree.** So: no shared helper, no new module, and the "four asserting absence" figure is void, having come from the same set.

**What the bad count nearly bought:** a new shared-util module, the tree's first local import across 50 zero-import specs, and a convention the Architecture Overview's Structural Inventory does not sanction — it maps `src/` and does not govern `test/`. I ran `structural-pre-flight` and concluded against the new file on those grounds *before* finding the count was wrong; that conclusion survives and is now also moot.

## Test Evidence
```
check-block-alignment.spec.mjs                 48 passed
  needle deliberately corrupted                exit 1 — "fixture mutation changed nothing —
                                               the needle has drifted out of SPLIT"  (47 passed, 1 failed)
full unit suite                                4119 passed, 2 skipped
```

The middle row is the one that matters. Without it this change is an assertion that has never been observed to fire, which is the same defect one level up.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**⛔ Retracting my own measurement, on the record, because this PR is where the correction belongs.** I claimed **12 mutation sites, 0 guarded**. Re-derived and classified in context:

```
dockRailTabLayering:72,122        selector normalisation (strip pseudo-elements, collapse whitespace)
dockSplitterLayering:56,57        stripping SCSS comments
dockSplitterLayering:173          path-prefix trim for a message string
esmDistTransforms:364,365         path rewriting
gitignoreNegationReachability:62 (×2), 67, 117   pattern normalisation
check-block-alignment:149         ← the ONLY fixture mutation
```

**One, not twelve.** My predicate was syntactic — `.replace(` — for a population that is semantic: *a mutation that plants a violation a checker must then catch*. Every other site transforms a string it is about to read, where a no-op needle changes nothing and asserts nothing. The ticket's Out of Scope had already excluded exactly that category, and my number walked straight through it.

**And my follow-up figure inherited the error.** I accepted *"four arms assert an ABSENCE"* as the sharpened subset; it was drawn from the same set, so it is void too. Both numbers are mine, and neither survives.

**The fix, verified rather than read.** Baseline **48 passed** at this head. Then the falsifier — I drifted the needle to a string absent from `SPLIT`:

```
Error: fixture mutation changed nothing — the needle has drifted out of SPLIT
  > 157 | expect(mutated, '…').not.toBe(SPLIT);
1 failed, 47 passed
```

Exactly the new assertion, nothing else, tree restored clean. **AC-3's "a guard against controls that cannot fail must not ship as one" is met, and I confirmed it independently.**

**`CONTROL:` semantics are intact.** `expect(status).toBe(0)` and `expect(output).not.toContain(...)` are unchanged; the arm simply cannot reach them against an unmutated fixture. The assertion is placed *before* `run()`, so a drifted needle reports drift rather than a confusing checker result.

- **Challenge, non-blocking:** the diff adds **6 comment lines to 3 code lines**, which is the ratio §pr_diff_equals_pr_body names as the cut signal — *added comment lines > added code lines ⇒ cut*. The assertion's own message already carries the *what* (`the needle has drifted out of SPLIT`), and the last two sentences — *"An arm expecting an ABSENCE cannot detect its own dead mutation from the outcome; only comparing against the source can"* — are the generalizable insight, which reads like commit-message or ticket material rather than file material. The first sentences earn their place because the assertion is genuinely non-obvious at the call site. I would cut to roughly half; I am not asking for it, because this file is the one place a future author is most likely to delete the assertion as redundant.
